claim: Portable computers become markedly lighter and thinner.
originalWording: Portable computers become markedly lighter and thinner.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 2, printed p. 12

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Portable computers are substantially lighter and thinner than typical 1999 notebooks; not every computer must shrink.
reference.rationale: The 2008 MacBook Air was three pounds and at most 0.76 inches thick; earlier PowerBooks provide a concrete size/weight comparator. Commercial thin laptops substantiate the direction and magnitude. A single earliest breakthrough year is unnecessary.

evidence.title: Apple unveils new PowerBook
evidence.note: Product-feature bullets: notebook weight with battery, and with DVD drive. The manufacturer lists 5.7 lb with a weight-saving module and 6.1 lb with the DVD drive. Evidence limits: Configuration-specific comparison, not a market-wide average.

evidence.title: Apple introduces MacBook Air
evidence.note: Opening product description; storage-options paragraph. The launch announcement specifies 0.16–0.76-inch thickness and describes hard-disk and optional SSD configurations. Evidence limits: This page does not give a three-pound weight; the added October 2008 source supplies that specification.

evidence.title: Apple unveils one-inch-thick Titanium PowerBook G4
evidence.note: Opening product description and thickness/weight feature bullets. Apple specifies a one-inch enclosure and 5.3 lb including battery and DVD drive. Evidence limits: A named model is a comparator, not proof of every notebook’s specifications.

evidence.title: Apple updates MacBook family (October 2008)
evidence.note: Paragraph announcing updates to MacBook Air and the 17-inch MacBook Pro. The October 2008 release explicitly specifies a three-pound MacBook Air and a maximum enclosure height of 0.76 inches. Evidence limits: This confirms the weight missing from the January release; it does not establish an exact first-achievement date.
